extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers of wartime dispatches (AP audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A compiled Associated Press wartime news article reporting on military operations, bombing raids, and lists/citations of military awards and decorations given for specific actions during World War II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished Flying Cross (DFC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for extraordinary achievement in action against the enemy; examples include pilots credited with sinking enemy ships, originating/new tactics (skip-bombing), or displaying gallantry under heavy antiaircraft and fighter opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page gives multiple examples of DFC citations: sinking a Japanese light cruiser/destroyer and cargo vessels; originating skip-bombing; flying at low altitude over Rabaul Harbor despite heavy antiaircraft fire; participation in dangerous operational flying (see example of Capt. Faul E. Cool receiving DFC for participating in more than 200 hours of dangerous operational flying). Use of DFC may cover both single acts of extraordinary achievement and sustained hazardous operational flying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguished Flying Medal / Distinguished Flying Medal citation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Conferred on aircrew for distinguished conduct in aerial operations; example citation notes number of sorties and steady, efficient conduct that contributed to safe return of the aircraft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Flight Sgt. Edmund Anthony Hinke received the Distinguished Flying Medal with citation noting 32 sorties and 'is a cool and efficient air gunner whose excellent work has on occasions contributed to the safe return' of his plane. Guidance implied: consistent exemplary performance over multiple sorties, actions that materially aided mission success or crew survival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air Medal
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for meritorious action against the enemy (air operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists recipients under the heading 'AIR MEDAL FOR MERITORIOUS ACTION AGAINST THE ENEMY' — implying the criterion is meritorious conduct in enemy-facing air missions. Many named enlisted and officer recipients are listed as examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Star
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page describes recipients receiving Silver Stars 'for gallantry in action over' specified engagements (e.g., over Buna, New Guinea). Also notes oak leaf clusters in lieu of a second Silver Star for repeat gallantry. Examples illustrate Silver Star attached to conspicuous bravery during aerial combat and protection of convoys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oak Leaf Cluster (as device for subsequent awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employed in lieu of a second award (e.g., an oak leaf cluster in lieu of a second Silver Star).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article references officers receiving an oak leaf cluster 'in lieu of a second Silver Star' to denote an additional instance of qualifying gallantry. Guidance: oak leaf cluster signifies subsequent awards rather than a distinct medal criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purple Heart
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally awarded for wounds received in action or for some exceptionally meritorious act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly states 'PURPLE HEARTS GENERALLY AWARDED FOR WOUNDS RECEIVED IN ACTION OR FOR SOME EXCEPTIONALLY MERITORIOUS ACT' and names officer recipients. Guidance: Purple Heart primarily recognizes combat wounds; the article signals occasional broader uses for exceptional merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soldiers' Medal
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for bravery not in combat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page includes the line 'SOLDIERS MEDAL FOR BRAVERY NOT IN COMBAT' and lists a recipient, indicating the Soldiers' Medal is intended to recognize non-combat heroism (i.e., valorous acts outside direct enemy engagement).
